answer: In an agent market trading goods such as quill pens, basalt tiles, and opal gems, each governance vote is weighted by tokens locked in escrow for 30 days. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand agent identities still yields only 100 tokens of voting weight. To gain more influence, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens, tying up capital and bearing price risk throughout the lock period; creating extra identities adds no power.
